note: From 11:13 to 1:00:30 the lesson is one long listening drill (Amal says a make-X / get-X verb, Medi glosses it in English), so D3-D27 are all mode=listening and stay apart. The two readers split systematically: r1 filed each misread as grammar with a bucket, r2 as vocab-A tier 1. READER-BRIEF says a form slip that a bucket rule names is grammar ("بسط for انبسط is GRAMMAR B12 not vocab"), so I ruled grammar wherever the misread piece is a form the buckets cover (B12 make/get, B1 b- present, B5 tense, B18 person prefix, D3/D4 endings, D1 preposition) and vocab only where the wrong piece is a different word or a word shape with no bucket (D1 nineteen, D2 dark). Names: Palestine, Spanish - never glossed. Engine notes: 38:59 'By all eight' = his بيتأسفوا; 42:47 he admits he heard منا for معنا; 32:24 'No.' is Medi's own line, not Amal's. Agreed rows A1-A10 all hold on the transcript - no challenges.

row.medi_said: This is it today. تسعة عشرين. ... uh, تسعة عشر. ... تسعش or تسعش. ... تسعش ستة.
row.amal_said: 19. ... 19 شو؟ ... تسعطاش تسعة.
row.right: تسعطاش
row.why: For the date 19 he produced three shapes that are not the dialect number (تسعة عشرين, MSA تسعة عشر, clipped تسعش); Amal prompted '19' and finally recast تسعطاش at 07:12 and he echoed it at 07:15 - a wrong form of a number he knows (sheet: nineteen | tese3ta3sh | تسعتاش), no bucket in buckets.md covers number shapes so it is vocab tier 2, not E4; one row for the whole 06:37-07:10 stretch, the ستة->تسعة part is agreed row A1.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same slip; the transcript supports vocab tier 2 (wrong form of a known word, no bucket names number shapes - E4 is days/months/'on Monday'). Timed at the first attempt 06:37 per the one-row rule.

row.medi_said: you took a photo or I, I take a photo? I had, had taken a photo? ... So it's اتصورت, right? ... It's اتصورت. There's no preposition.
row.amal_said: صورت. ... Is it did you take a photo or did you get-- did you take a photo of yourself؟ Like, did you get photographed؟ Which one is it؟

row.why: He read her t- form tsawwaret (get photographed) as the make-X صوّر (take a photo); Amal contrasted صورت and prompted take-vs-get until he said 'I got photographed' at 12:10 and she said حلو - make-X vs get-X is B12, so grammar, not a different word.

rulings.why: Both readers found it; kind differs. The misread is the make/get form of one root, which READER-BRIEF files as grammar B12.

row.why: Her ta33abetni (you made me tired, object -ni) he read as te3ebt minni (you got tired of me); Amal said 'No, that's تعبت مني' and repeated تعبتني, then prompted the tense until he said 'You tired me' at 13:10 - make-X vs get-X (B12) with the object ending (D4).

row.medi_said: He will not, he will not bore you.

row.english: he will not be bored of you

rulings.why: Only r1 found it. It is a supplied phrase answering his 'how would X go' (tier 0 didn't-know), so it belongs on his page but unscored; the bucket r1 put on it is removed because vocab rows take no bucket.

row.medi_said: so don't be tired of me.

row.medi_said: She laughed at him.

row.right: at me (علي)

row.right: who made you upset (ضايق = make upset)
row.why: Her مين ضايقك (who made you upset) he first read as 'who was he mad at you' and then glossed daaya2 as 'to be upset'; Amal prompted ضايق vs اتضايق and he worked out 'ضايق is to make someone upset ... who made you upset?' at 28:17 - make-X vs get-X, B12; one row timed at his first misread 27:44.

Self-fix before help: for ما تعصبني he said 'Don't be angry at me or don't make me angry' in one breath - the right reading was already his before Amal spoke; her 'mm-hmm. Don't make me angry' confirms the second half rather than correcting him (no 'no', no contrast). Not a slip.

I made him happy' at 32:46 and she said ممتاز - B12. The 'No.' at 32:24 is Medi's own line, so the signal is prompt-then-fix, not explicit-no.
